messages.content: Help me add a 'click' event listener to a button element 'myButton' that triggers a function named 'handleButtonClick' and stops the event from propagating by setting options's stopProgation to true?

function.name: buttonAddClickHandler
function.description: This function attaches a click event listener to a specified button element with options to control event flow and behavior. Note that the provided function is in JavaScript syntax.

element.description: The button element to which the event listener will be added. This parameter can be of any type of JavaScript object in string representation.

callback.description: The function to be called when the button is clicked. This parameter can be of any type of JavaScript object in string representation.

options.description: An options object to specify characteristics about the event listener, such as stopping propagation. Optional parameter. Default to be empty dictionary This is JavaScript dict type parameter in string representation.

message.reasoning:
We need to use the function buttonAddClickHandler. Provide element: "myButton" (string). callback: "handleButtonClick". options: {stopPropagation: true}. Note: The options key is spelled stopProgation? The user wrote stopProgation (typo). But we should correct to stopPropagation. But maybe they want the exact property name. The function signature says options?: string, a JavaScript dict type parameter in string representation. So we need to pass a JSON string? The function expects string representation of the object. So we need to pass something like '{"stopPropagation":true}'. The element is string representation of the button element. Could be "document.getElementById('myButton')" or just "myButton"? The description: "The button element to which the event listener will be added. This parameter can be of any type of JavaScript object in string representation." So we can pass "document.getElementById('myButton')". The callback: "handleButtonClick". So we call the function.

Thus we need to produce a function call: functions.buttonAddClickHandler({element:"document.getElementById('myButton')", callback:"handleButtonClick", options:"{\"stopPropagation\":true}"})
